It is the plural of *uftu'ulah* from the word *qawl* (saying), like *al-adahik*, the plural of *udhuka* (a joke), not the plural of *aqwal* (sayings), so that it would be a plural of a plural, because it would then follow that he would not be punished for fewer than three [sayings -].

Surely We would have seized him (﴿لأخَذْنا﴾), that is, with Our majesty, a seizing of might, wrath, subjugation and destruction. He emphasized it to make known the intensity of Our anger at lying and the intensity of its ugliness.

Since His seizing is a seizing before which every other seizing vanishes, for whoever fabricates against kings receives from them nothing but this, He said: ﴿by the right hand﴾ (﴿مِنهُ﴾, that is, specifically), that is, ﴿with the right﴾ (﴿بِاليَمِينِ﴾), which is the strongest limb, for it is with it that one's grip is exercised, so We would remove him by the intensity of Our grip; or "the right" refers to Us, and it is then a metaphor for Our seizing him with utmost power. For the strength of every thing lies in its right side. It has also been said that when a king wishes to humiliate a person he says, "Take him, O so-and-so," and the man seizes him by the right hand; this is then a metaphor for abasement. It has also been said that this depicts execution by beheading in its most grievous form: when a king wishes to lighten matters for the one he is going to kill, he orders the executioner, and the executioner seizes the condemned man's left hand with his own left hand and strikes with the sword from behind him, because the neck from behind is wider, so the cut is quicker, and the condemned man does not see the gleam of the sword. [But if the king wishes torment and extreme humiliation, he seizes the condemned man's right hand with his own left hand and strikes him while he faces him, so that he sees the gleam of the sword.] Perhaps the blow falls, owing to the narrowness of space from the front, upon his jaw, so that a second and third blow are needed, and this is the most shameful of all.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 69, verse 46:

Having depicted the beginning of the destruction in its most dreadful form, He completed it, indicating the severity of its horror by the particle of delay (*thumma*), saying: ﴿Then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾, decisively and without any hesitation, with the cutting of Our greatness, before which every other cutting vanishes. ﴿The aorta (al-Watin, الوتين)﴾, that is, the greatest vein in the neck, the firm, enduring, strong vessel called the *al-warid* (الوريد), which lies between the *al-'ilba'* (العلباء) and the *al-hulqum* (الحلقوم). It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that it is *niyat al-qalb* (نياط القلب), the ligaments of the heart. In *al-Qamus* (the lexicon): a vein in the heart; if it is severed, its owner dies. The expression was chosen for it because its root, in this arrangement, revolves around firmness and permanence, and so its owner perishes when it is lost.

Ibn Burjan said: it is a vein connected to the *niyat al-qalb*, lying along the spine, filling the whole body. The liver, which is the house of the blood, supplies it, and blood flows from it throughout the body. Sixty veins take from it; these are the rivers of blood throughout the whole body. Of these rivers, eighteen take from it to the body, seven supply the eye, four supply the brain. The *al-watin* runs from the junction of the two hips to the junction of the chest, between the two collarbones, and from it all the other veins branch out to the rest of the body. Life is not normally possible after its severance. And in al-Ma'idah, at His saying ﴿Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], there is what is useful here. (p-382)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 69, verse 47:

When he had completed the depiction of what kings do to those with whom they are angry, namely that one of their agents seizes him by the right hand and restrains him, like the sword that strikes off his neck, He made the following statement a consequence of this, completing His greatness with His saying: ﴿So there is not among you﴾, that is, O people, "and he intensified the negation, so he said: ﴿anyone who could withhold Us from him﴾, that is, from the killing or from the one who is killed, the transmitted [-] ..." And since "anyone" (aḥad) is general, He specified its generality by describing it, and He spoke of "among you" (minkum) in the Hijazi usage of "mā" with His saying: ﴿restraining﴾, that is, it would be a restraining, decisive, dense barrier preventing access to Him. So no purpose connected with a rational person would lead him to advise anyone with advice that returns benefit to the one advised alone, and there is no stake for the speaker [in it -] in a lie that burdens himself to fabricate it against a king whom the one advised cannot protect from his punishment for that lie. He chose the report in the plural because it indicates that no single individual can restrain Him, a fortiori (min bāb al-ūlā). "Among you" (minkum) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) because it is fronted. All of this is a kināya, in the most eloquent manner, that this Reminder is the speech of Allah, with no doubt whatsoever, combined with the aspects of its inimitability. For "law" (law) indicates the impossibility of the second because of the impossibility of the first, so the estimation, as is said in the istithnā'ī syllogism, is: "We would not have seized him in this manner; therefore it is established that he did not fabricate anything against Us. Thus it is established [that -] what he said is Our speech with complete establishment, by proof in a manner that cannot be overturned."

(p-383) Since this was a metaphor (kināya) for that, without regard to the literal meanings of its individual words or the meaning of any one of them taken separately, it was as if it had been said: "A revelation from the Lord of the worlds, in which falsehood cannot be imagined in any way." He then joined to that His saying: ﴿And indeed it﴾, that is, the Qur'an, after it had been a reminder for all the worlds, ﴿is surely a reminder﴾, that is, a reminder of very great magnitude, ﴿for the God-fearing﴾, that is, from among the worlds, because they are the ones who benefit from it, by their turning to it with the eagerness of one seeking benefit.

When he knew from this that He, glory be to Him, has knowledge of both categories of the evildoer and the good person, outwardly and inwardly, He made explicit the other category, saying, emphasizing it to refute misguidance: ﴿And indeed We﴾, that is, with the greatness that belongs to Us, ﴿surely know﴾, that is, with a great [encompassing] knowledge, ﴿that among you﴾, O earthly, lowly people, who lack the capacity for elevation to the stripping of souls from the dense attachments of the body, ﴿are deniers﴾, that is, deeply immersed in denial. Therefore We sent down the Books and dispatched the Messengers, so that there would become manifest from you, into the world of witnessing, what We had been bringing about in eternity as something unseen, of denial and belief, and thereby you would deserve punishment or reward. For this reason, in the wisdom which no one denies and no one doubts is the distinctive attribute of the King who manifests perfection, it was necessary that He restore creation to what they had been in their bodies before death, so that We may judge between them and recompense each one (p-384) with what befits him, manifesting justice.

Since the cause of their denial was the concealing of what the clear-sighted intellects would reveal of the proofs, and the implied sense was: "Indeed it is good tidings for the believers," but He withheld this because the context is the warning about al-Haqqah (the Inevitable Reality), He joined to it His saying, emphasizing what they have of denial of it:

﴿And indeed it﴾, that is, the Great Qur'an, ﴿is a cause of anguish﴾, that is, by what they see of its consequence in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, that is, those deeply immersed in disbelief, because they denied it, owing to what will become manifest to them of their recompense and the recompense of the believers.

Since each of the two groups is tasting its recompense in the Hereafter, and since everyone who has heard the Qur'an has realized that they cannot produce anything like it or come near to it, He said, emphasizing it and placing them among the ignorant: ﴿And indeed it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an or the recompense on the Day of Recompense, ﴿is the truth of certainty﴾, i.e., the established matter which, once tasted, becomes [no longer] open to doubt; it is therefore certainty affirmed by the Truth. It is an idafa of the attribute to the thing described, and it is above "the knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqīn). In this there is an indication that the servant should attain, for this, knowledge of the Truth, so that he witnesses the unseen as one witnesses visible things, by what he observes of their like. The matter of resurrection is witnessed every day in the night and the day, and every year in vegetation and other things.

[p. 385]

When resurrection, for this purpose, was among the greatest of perfections, and its absence necessitated deficiency, He tied both matters together by indication and expression in His saying, commanding after the report at the beginning of the *Musabbihat* (the surahs that begin with glorification of God, *tasbih*): ﴿So glorify﴾, meaning: perform the complete declaration of transcendence above every trace of deficiency, ﴿in the name of﴾, meaning: by means of your knowledge of the attributes of ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who brings you into being, nurtures you, and bestows upon you kindness of every kind, ﴿the Mighty﴾, whose greatness has filled all the regions entirely, and has exceeded that by what He wills, glorified is He, of what minds cannot contain. This is especially so regarding their saying that He will not restore us. He, glorified and exalted is He, is Able to do that, nothing can overpower Him, and He has promised it, and He is true to His promise. The absence of resurrection would violate wisdom, given the wrongdoing of most people. There is in this an indication of disengagement (*mutarakah*), and a marvelling at their condition in their insistence upon falsehood and obstinacy, and their stubbornness in disputation and corruption. Thus, at the end of the surah, it returns to its beginning with the realization of the Inevitable Reality (*ihqaq al-haqqah*), to negate what was confused in the abode of concealment behind causes, from the places of deficiency and the sources of confusion. So the truth is established, falsehood is negated, and a distinction is made between the good-doer and the wrongdoer, the happy and the wretched. Thus peace is due to the party of the Merciful, and destruction is established for the companions of Satan, and His Manifest Name becomes evident to every believer and unbeliever. ﴿Indeed, in that is a lesson for people of understanding﴾. And God is the Guide.
